> I'm not a big fan of editing the lockfile this way, especially when there can be multiple versions of it and what if we need to handle for more package manager in the future. 

That's why I have hesitated to do anything about it for so long.

> It'd be nice if Changesets starts moving towards being package manager agnostic so we don't have to maintain a lot of specific code.

In theory, yes - I agree. In practice, it feels like we already have some other code specific to package managers (even when publishing packages). And this would just make this more usable to npm users. 

> I think we should try to tackle this differently, maybe a post-step to automatically call npm i or document it?

As to the documentation, I think it would just be a chore for people to always have to learn about the need to do this when they are using npm. Ideally, things "should just work" and be user-friendly and I feel relying on the docs here wouldn't be that.

`npm i` also has some footguns. If called incorrectly, it could touch unrelated parts of the lockfile and, ideally, only the parts relevant to `changeset version` should change. Then if u'd have some accidental lockfile mismatch on CI it would still fail for legitimate reasons on `--frozen-lockfile` (or similar)

> In theory, yes - I agree. In practice, it feels like we already have some other code specific to package managers (even when publishing packages). And this would just make this more usable to npm users.

But do we want to move towards making things more agnostic? We do have the specific code for publishing packages now, but if we agree, I'd like to try to generalize it again. But if this PR goes through, it'll cause another breaking change, or at least subtle differences.

EDIT: Also, maybe being agnostic isn't the accurate wording here, but more "reduced package-manager-specific handling surface".

> `npm i` also has some footguns. If called incorrectly, it could touch unrelated parts of the lockfile and, ideally, only the parts relevant to `changeset version` should change. Then if u'd have some accidental lockfile mismatch on CI it would still fail for legitimate reasons on `--frozen-lockfile` (or similar)

If they're applying a release plan and the lockfile is unstable, I think there's a bigger issue there. If we update anyways, the user would still have to later run `npm i` or something to stabilize the lockfile. So FWICT we should be able to assume that it's stable.

If we do want to go with manual updating the lockfile, it might be better move the code as a separate package/repo I think, so it's easier to test with different package managers in CI and if other lockfile formats need edits too.

There's an existing PR that does similar changes too: #1455

And there's also an existing issue about this: #1139
Is there an ETA on this?

> If they're applying a release plan and the lockfile is unstable, I think there's a bigger issue there. If we update anyways, the user would still have to later run `npm i` or something to stabilize the lockfile. So FWICT we should be able to assume that it's stable.

Hi, @bluwy!

Thanks again for the clarification.

In my case the lockfile is stable, but my CI workflows use `npm ci`. After `changeset version` updates versions in `package.json`, the lockfile becomes out of sync, so the generated `Version Packages` PR fails in CI unless `package-lock.json` is updated as part of the process.

I used the workaround suggested by @mikeybinns and called `npm install` from the `changeset:version` script (`"changeset:version": "changeset version && npm install && git add --all"`). In my case that seems to update only the relevant version entries in `package-lock.json` and solves the CI issue.

I understand the concern about increasing the package-manager-specific surface area, so I am not trying to push for a particular implementation. I mainly wanted to share that this npm + `npm ci` case does come up in practice, even with an otherwise stable lockfile.

I think it could be helpful to document the recommended workaround for npm users. Since this is typically wired directly into the `changeset:version` script, it might also help to mention that users may want to add a check ensuring that `npm install` only changes the expected version-related entries in `package-lock.json` before running `git add --all`.

Thank you!

Konstantin

title: Added an automatic update for `package-lock.json` content when applying the release plan
